newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on tight liquidity.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Saturday as troubles at the Kia Group led to a tightening in overall market liquidity, brokers said.
"Sentiment chilled again due to tightening liquidity. Further consolidation is likely next week," said Kim Choon-kwon of Daewoo Securities.
The composite index ended 5.22 points lower at 742.15.
Brokers said interest rates were on the rise since local banks decided to bail out the troubled Kia Group on Tuesday.
Yields for three-year corporate bonds rose to 12.13 percent on Saturday from 11.75 percent a week earlier.
Volume totalled 24.49 million shares for Saturday's half-day trading, compared with 40.98 million on Friday.
Losers outpaced gainers 497 to 261 with 130 unchanged.
Brokers said the index would test the 720 level next week.
"It will take time for the market to recover from the Kia shock," said Na Min-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities.
Kia Motors, the carmaking flagship of the Kia Group, gained 800 won to 12,300 after a sharp fall earlier this week. -- KIM MYONG-HWAN (822) 727 5645
